The brand should feel private, on-device, alive, and precise rather than decorative.\n\n## Core visual rules\n\n- Backgrounds stay near-black with deep blue-violet undertones.\n- The assistant mark emits warm light from its core, shifting toward cool blue and violet at the edge.\n- Light should originate from the assistant itself, not from external UI decoration.\n- Use soft radial illumination, not heavy neon outlines.\n- Surfaces are translucent dark glass with subtle borders.\n- The wordmark is quiet, rounded, and technical.\n\n## Palette\n\n| Token | Hex | Purpose |\n|---|---:|---|\n| Midnight | `#03040A` | deepest background |\n| Deep Space | `#06080D` | primary dark field |\n| Ink | `#090B12` | elevated dark surfaces |\n| Lumen | `#FFEAA3` | assistant light core |\n| Ember | `#FFC75C` | warm source color |\n| Corona | `#A3CCFF` | cool halo |\n| Plasma | `#788FFF` | technical blue accent |\n| Violet | `#A36EFF` | peripheral glow |\n\n## Included assets\n\n- `lumen-assistant-mark.png` — square app-mark source.\n- `lumen-vertical-logo.png` — vertical logo lockup source.\n- `lumen-wordmark-lockup.png` — horizontal logo lockup source.\n- `LumenBrand.swift` — native SwiftUI brand components.\n\n## SwiftUI components\n\n- `LumenAssistantMark`\n- `LumenBrandBackground`\n- `LumenLightBeam`\n\nThese are preferred in-app because they scale cleanly and preserve dynamic illumination without raster assets.", "title": "ios/Lumen/Brand/BRANDING.md"}

Future changes mu\n\n## Strategic context: unified-memory inference is a physical constraint\n\niOS devices use a unified memory architecture. The app heap, Metal buffers, llama.cpp runtime state, KV cache, and adapter weights all compete for the same physical memory budget. The Apple Neural Engine (ANE) is not used by the current GGU\n\nDocumentation is therefore part of the runtime safety system. It explains why the code must prefer rigid adapter sequencing over clever shortcuts.\n\n---\n\n## Resolution 1: single-adapter stacking guard\n\n### Poison: PR 171 adapter overlap failure\n\nThe historical failure mode was role switching without a hard adapter clear. Switching Cortex, Executor, Mouth, Mimicry, or REM while a previous LoRA remained active could leave overlapping matrices in the shared model context.
